_doc: The edit decision list for film/build/edit.py. Captions are templates filled from facts.json ({key}); a caption
with a figure that isn't a fact fails the build. Times are seconds of film time. A time may name a mark in the
beat's events.json instead: 'name', 'name=value' (any data field), '#n' for the nth match (1-based), then an
optional offset ('scrub-start+0.4', 'end'). Caption times are relative to the beat's output; segment in/out
are capture times. A value given as {"16x9": …, "9x16": …} differs by aspect. Speed ≠ 1 shows a ×N badge.
'band': 'top-right' moves a beat's caption box off the UI it would cover (16:9 only; 9:16 captions sit below the app).
Credit chips come from the capture's 'clip' marks (the engines whose clips are in view). The loop has no
overlays, so it must come from a stretch with no clip playing (P01: the Tax drag; P10: the results, which name the models).

Narration: each caption is also a spoken line ('say' if the spoken form differs; 'show': false for a line read over a card whose text is already on screen). With voice files in film/vo/, lines play in order from their 'from' time, never overlapping, and each subtitle stays up until the next line starts; 'to' is used only for a silent cut.

card.title: Is the stability score measuring stability, or stillness?
card.sub: {n_clips_total} generated clips, each beside the hand-drawn still it was made from.

captions.text: Wan 2.2 wins on stability. But it barely moved.
captions.say: Wan wins on stability. But it barely moved.
So is the score measuring stability, or stillness?

captions.text: Pick a panel and an engine.
Asked to stay idle, its lines drift anyway.
Scrub the curve and the clip follows. It plots how far the line art has moved from frame 0.
captions.say: Scrub the curve and the clip follows. It plots how far the line art has moved from the first frame.

captions.text: The difference view shows the change itself. Black means unchanged.
More motion goes with more drift: ρ {rho} across {n_engines} engines, p {p_exact}.
captions.say: More motion goes with more drift: rho {rho} across {n_engines} engines, p {p_exact}.

captions.text: So try an exploratory lens: charge each engine for its motion.
At price 0, it's the paper's ranking: Wan 2.2 leads. Now raise the price.
captions.say: At zero, it's the paper's ranking: Wan leads. Now raise the price.

captions.text: From {x_g45} px per doubling of motion, Gen-4.5 leads.
captions.say: From {x_g45} pixels per doubling of motion, Gen four point five leads.

captions.text: Its rank changes because it moves more, not because it looks better.

card.title: Price the motion in, and the ranking becomes a choice you can see.
card.sub: A case for evaluating world models with motion priced in, not on stability alone.

captions.say: Price the motion in, and the ranking becomes a choice you can see. A case for evaluating world models with motion priced in, not on stability alone.

voice.design: Someone who builds things, showing a friend what surprised them. Conversational, quick-witted, curious and a little wry; confident without selling. Grounded and direct with some texture in the voice, never soft, breathy or announcer-polished. Natural rhythm, a smile you can hear, no upward inflection at the ends of lines.
